impact: About 4,000 retired New York City municipal employees had names, health and financial data in a copayment-refund claims database accessed; no payments were reportedly altered.
date_note: Date of the Infobae report of a Politico exclusive; the access itself was on 20 September and 5 to 8 October 2026.
title: Claims database for retired New York City employees accessed by unknown user at administrator Atticus
org: Atticus Administration (for New York City retirees)
summary: Infobae, citing a Politico exclusive, reports that an unknown user accessed the claims database of Atticus Administration, which handles copayment refunds for retired New York City employees. Per a 14 October letter, access happened on 20 September and between 5 and 8 October, exposing names, health and financial data for about 4,000 retirees. The letter says no payments were created, modified or redirected. No attacker has been identified.
plain: A company refunding health copayments to retired New York City workers had its claims database accessed by an unknown person. About 4,000 retirees' health and financial details were exposed.
exec: A third-party administrator breach exposed government retirees' health and financial data; vendor access controls and fraud checks matter.
action: Affected retirees: watch for the notification letter, monitor accounts and health insurance statements, and consider a credit freeze.

key_findings: Unknown user accessed the claims database on 20 September and periodically between 5 and 8 October, per a letter dated 14 October.
Data included names, health data, financial information, copayment amounts, provider names and internal IDs; about 4,000 retirees affected.
Atticus says no payment to claimants was created, modified or redirected; its investigation is ongoing.

validation.note: One article (Infobae), itself reporting a Politico exclusive; Politico and the letter not read.
